assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: R-group
items.clue: The variable side chain of an amino acid.

items.label: Amphipathic
items.clue: Describes a molecule that has both a hydrophilic (water-attracting) region and a hydrophobic (water-excluded) region.

items.label: Lipid
items.clue: A substance in living organisms that dissolves in non-polar solvents but is only sparingly soluble in aqueous (water-based) solvents.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly links a property of glucose to the way it is used in organisms?

options.text: Glucose breaks down readily on its own, which is why it is used as a respiratory substrate
Glucose dissolves in water because its molecules are small, so it is easily transported
Glucose is highly soluble, so cells store large quantities of it dissolved in their cytoplasm
Glucose is chemically stable, so it is transported in blood plasma without breaking down

questions.stem: Liver cells store glucose in the form of glycogen. Why is the glucose not simply stored as free glucose?

options.text: Glycogen is relatively insoluble because of its size, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
Glycogen is insoluble because it is non-polar, so it stays separate from the watery cytoplasm
The branches of glycogen make its glucose hard to remove, so the store is not used up too quickly
Glycogen stores extra energy in the glycosidic bonds that link its glucose monomers together

questions.stem: Cellulose gives plant cell walls high tensile strength. Which feature of cellulose is responsible for this?

options.text: The glycosidic bonds within cellulose are very much stronger than those within starch
The chains coil into tight helices that stretch and recoil like a spring
Beta-glucose is a larger monomer than alpha-glucose, giving thicker chains
Straight chains lie side by side in bundles, cross-linked by many hydrogen bonds

questions.stem: The ABO blood groups depend on glycoproteins on the surface of red blood cells. Which statement about these ABO antigens is correct?

options.text: The A and B antigens differ only in the sugar at the end of their carbohydrate chain
The A and B antigens are two entirely different proteins with unrelated amino acid sequences
Group O red blood cells carry a third antigen, the O antigen, in the place of the A or B
The carbohydrate part of each antigen projects inwards into the cell's cytoplasm

questions.stem: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid molecules react by condensation to form one triglyceride. How much water is produced?

options.text: One water molecule is released
Four water molecules are released
No water is released; water is used up
Three water molecules are released

questions.explanation: Each of the three hydroxyl groups of glycerol reacts with the carboxyl group of one fatty acid in a separate condensation reaction, forming an ester bond and releasing one water molecule, so three water molecules are released in total.

questions.stem: Which property of triglycerides makes them well suited to long-term energy storage in adipose tissue?

options.text: They release less energy per gram than carbohydrates, so a store of them lasts longer
They are very large molecules, so they cannot dissolve and leave the adipose cell
They release about twice the energy per gram of carbohydrates when oxidized
Their many ester bonds store energy that is released when the bonds are broken

questions.explanation: Triglycerides yield roughly twice the energy per gram of carbohydrate, and they are stored without the water that accompanies glycogen and without osmotic effects, so a great deal of energy is held in a small, stable mass, which is what a long-term store needs.

questions.stem: Four molecules are drawn as molecular diagrams. Which description identifies the molecule that is a steroid?

options.text: A single six-membered ring made up of five carbon atoms and one oxygen atom
A chain of amino acids folded up into a compact globular shape
Four fused rings of carbon atoms, three with six atoms and one with five
A glycerol backbone joined to three long hydrocarbon chains

questions.explanation: A steroid is recognized by its four fused rings sharing edges, three six-membered and one five-membered. Oestradiol and testosterone both have this structure, which is non-polar and lets them pass through the phospholipid bilayer.

questions.stem: Which feature is shared by all 20 of the amino acids that are coded for in the genetic code?

options.text: An amine group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen atom and an R-group are all bonded to one alpha carbon atom.
The R-group is identical in every amino acid, and the amine and carboxyl groups are what vary.
The amine group is bonded directly to the carbon atom of the carboxyl group, with no carbon between.
The amine group is an NH₃ group, with the same structure as a molecule of ammonia.

questions.stem: A polypeptide of 150 amino acids is assembled by condensation reactions. How does the number of water molecules change as the whole chain is formed?

options.text: 150 released
300 released
149 released
149 consumed

questions.explanation: Each condensation reaction links two amino acids with one peptide bond and releases one molecule of water. Joining 150 amino acids into one chain needs 149 peptide bonds, so 149 water molecules are released.

questions.stem: What is meant by an essential amino acid?

options.text: One that the body needs in larger quantities than the non-essential amino acids.
One of the 20 amino acids, all of which must be supplied by the protein in the diet.
One that is found in animal protein but is absent from all plant-based foods.
One that cannot be synthesized in the body and must be obtained from food.

questions.explanation: This is the definition: essential amino acids cannot be synthesized and must be obtained from food, whereas non-essential amino acids can be made from other amino acids.

questions.stem: Why is the number of different possible polypeptides described as effectively infinite?

options.text: The 20 amino acids can be arranged in any order, but each amino acid can be used only once in a given chain.
There are very many combinations of amino acids, and the order of the amino acids does not affect the protein.
Chains can be of any length, and the 20 amino acids can occur in any order and be used any number of times.
Each extra amino acid added to a chain adds 20 to the number of different polypeptides that are possible.

questions.stem: When egg white is heated, its soluble proteins turn into a white solid. What has happened to the protein molecules?

options.text: Heat has broken the peptide bonds, so the polypeptides have been split into amino acids.
Heat has killed the proteins, so they are no longer able to carry out their functions.
Heat has changed their shape temporarily, and they will refold as soon as the egg white cools.
Heat has broken the bonds holding their folded shape, so they have unfolded.
